content: Insulin lispro is a medication prescribed to help manage blood sugar levels in individuals with diabetes. It belongs to a class of drugs known as hormones. People with diabetes often do not produce sufficient natural insulin, which is essential for metabolizing carbohydrates, fats, and proteins from food and for transporting sugar from the bloodstream to other parts of the body. Insulin lispro acts as a replacement for the insulin that the body would normally produce. It has a rapid onset of action but a shorter duration of effect compared to regular insulin. This medication is always used in combination with other diabetes treatments, which may include other types of insulin or oral medications, depending on the specific type of diabetes. Insulin lispro is available as a liquid solution for subcutaneous injection (under the skin). It is typically administered 15 minutes before a meal or immediately after eating. Your doctor will determine the number of daily injections you require. It is crucial to follow the instructions on your prescription label precisely and consult your doctor or pharmacist if you have any questions. Do not use more or less of the medication or administer it more frequently than prescribed. Never use insulin lispro if you are experiencing symptoms of hypoglycemia (low blood sugar) or if your blood sugar levels are low, as confirmed by testing. In such cases, contact your doctor immediately. While insulin lispro helps control diabetes, it does not cure the condition. You should continue using it even if you feel well and should not stop without consulting your doctor. Do not switch to a different brand or type of insulin or alter the dosage of any insulin you are using without medical advice. Insulin lispro is available in various forms, including vials, cartridges for use in dosing pens, and pre-filled dosing pens. If your insulin lispro is supplied in vials, you will need syringes marked U-100 for accurate dosing. If your insulin lispro comes in cartridges, you will need to purchase a compatible insulin pen. Refer to the manufacturer's instructions to determine the correct pen for your cartridge size, and ask your doctor or pharmacist for guidance on its use. If you are using a pre-filled pen, carefully read and follow the manufacturer's instructions, and always prime the pen before use. Never attempt to remove the cartridge from the pen or mix other types of insulin into the cartridge. Do not reuse or share needles, syringes, cartridges, or pens. If you are using an insulin pen, remove the needle immediately after injecting your dose and dispose of it in a puncture-resistant container. Consult your doctor or pharmacist for proper disposal methods. Your doctor may instruct you to mix insulin lispro with another type of insulin in the same syringe. If so, always draw insulin lispro into the syringe first, use the same brand of syringe, and inject the mixture immediately after preparation. Insulin lispro can be injected into the thighs, abdomen, or upper arms. Rotate injection sites, ensuring each new injection is at least half an inch away from the previous site. Do not use the medication if it appears discolored, cloudy, thickened, or contains solid particles, or if it is past its expiration date. To prepare a dose from a vial, follow these steps: 1. Wash your hands thoroughly. 2. If using a new vial, remove the plastic cap but leave the stopper intact. 3. Clean the vial's rubber stopper with an alcohol swab. 4. Pull back the syringe plunger to the dose your doctor prescribed. 5. Insert the needle into the vial's stopper and push the plunger to inject air into the vial. 6. Turn the vial upside down, ensuring the needle tip remains submerged in the liquid. 7. Slowly pull back the plunger to draw the prescribed dose into the syringe. 8. Check for air bubbles in the syringe. If present, tap the syringe to move the bubbles to the top, then push the plunger to expel them and redraw the correct dose. 9. Remove the needle from the vial and place the syringe on a clean surface, ensuring the needle does not touch anything. To inject insulin lispro using a syringe or pen: 1. Clean the injection site with an alcohol swab. 2. Pinch or spread the skin at the injection site. 3. Insert the needle as instructed by your doctor. 4. If using a syringe, push the plunger down completely. If using a pen, follow the manufacturer's instructions. 5. Remove the needle and press on the injection site for several seconds without rubbing. Before using insulin lispro, inform your doctor and pharmacist if you are allergic to insulin or any other medications. Provide a complete list of all prescription and nonprescription medications, vitamins, supplements, and herbal products you are taking, as some may interact with insulin lispro. Notify your doctor if you have a history of nerve damage caused by diabetes, adrenal, pituitary, or thyroid disorders, or liver or kidney disease. If you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding, inform your doctor. If you become pregnant while using insulin lispro, contact your doctor immediately. Additionally, inform your healthcare provider if you are undergoing surgery, including dental procedures, or if you experience illness, stress, changes in activity levels, or travel across time zones, as these factors may affect your insulin requirements. Follow your doctor's dietary recommendations, maintain a consistent eating schedule, and avoid skipping or delaying meals. Alcohol can lower blood sugar levels, so consult your doctor about safe alcohol consumption while using insulin lispro. If you miss a dose, inject it as soon as you remember, provided it is shortly before or after a meal. If significant time has passed, contact your doctor for guidance. Do not inject a double dose to compensate for a missed one. Insulin lispro may cause side effects, including changes in blood sugar levels. Be aware of the symptoms of hypoglycemia (e.g., shakiness, dizziness, sweating, irritability, hunger, or confusion) and hyperglycemia (e.g., extreme thirst, frequent urination, blurred vision, or weakness). Severe hypoglycemia or hyperglycemia can lead to life-threatening conditions, so seek immediate medical attention if necessary. Other side effects may include redness, swelling, or itching at the injection site. Rare but serious side effects include rash, difficulty breathing, hives, or changes in skin texture. Report any unusual symptoms to your doctor. Store insulin lispro in its original container, tightly closed, and out of reach of children. Refrigerate vials, pens, and cartridges not in use, but do not freeze them. The vial or pen in use can be stored at room temperature in a cool, dark place for up to 28 days. Dispose of expired or unused medication properly, and consult your pharmacist for disposal instructions. In case of overdose, contact a poison control center or emergency services immediately. Overdose symptoms may include severe hypoglycemia, seizures, or coma. Keep all medical appointments and follow your doctor's instructions for monitoring your blood sugar levels.
